findings.title: Wait for the old flusher to exit before starting its replacement
findings.body: `Process.kill()` only sends a termination signal; it does not wait for the process to stop. The replacement is started immediately afterward, so a hung flusher that is still executing Redis or Kafka operations can overlap with its replacement. Both may flush the same segment and produce it to Kafka, causing duplicate buffered segments. Join the killed process before starting the replacement.

findings.title: Reject non-positive flusher process counts
findings.body: This option accepts zero and negative values, but `SpanFlusher` uses the configured value to determine how many workers to create. With a negative value, `num_processes` is negative and the worker map is empty, so no process flushes buffered spans; with zero, the fallback currently masks the invalid value and silently creates a different worker count. Validate that `--flusher-processes` is positive so invalid configuration cannot leave spans unflushed or behave unexpectedly.
